transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-08 15:00 UTC / Duration: ~45m / Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Myers (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM); Dr. Maya Chen, Carlos Ruiz, Aisha Bello, Tariq Malik (Sable).

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for taking the time. we wanted to run through the postmortem for the 9/3 outage and make sure we have an aligned remediation plan. Maya, thanks for joining.
[00:14] Maya: thanks Jordan. yeah this has been pretty painful for us, customers noticed timeouts on inference calls at high qps; some calls returned 500s. we lost a few real-time pipelines.
[00:27] Jordan: understood, and really sorry about the impact. quick agenda: timeline review, root cause hypotheses, immediate mitigations we can apply, verification plan, and then SLA remediation / credits. does that look ok?
[00:38] Aisha: yes that's good. also we'd like to understand why the fallback to lower-tier model didn't kick in for some requests.
[00:44] Priya: ok we'll cover that. quick note, the transcript's gonna have some noise, some of our internal names might be mucked up (eg KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cash).
[00:53] Jordan: timeline — on 2026-09-03 at ~18:10 UTC we saw a spike in seq length and token output for two routes, followed by elevated tail latency and 5xx errors starting ~18:12 and peaking 18:15 to 18:28. Autoscaler attempted to add nodes at 18:16 but some of the new instances registered with degraded health causing routing thrash. by 18:30 the system stabilized after an automatic fallback to the model variant and a manual kill of two unhealthy workers.
[01:20] Carlos: quick question — was there a deployment at that time? we have nothing on our side.
[01:26] Priya: we looked at deploy logs — no deploys in that window. there was a scheduled background job on Sable side that ran at ~18:07 which increased request size/seq length, so that likely contributed.
[01:35] Maya: correct, an ETL job pushed larger batched prompts to our inference route.
[01:39] Jordan: root cause hypothesis 1: KV cache eviction + cold starts. with the sudden sequence length and memory pressure, the runtime evicted prefix cache entries and those requests incurred full context recompute causing latency amplification and queueing. hypothesis 2: autoscaler jitter — newly provisioned GPU nodes failed health checks due to transient driver OOMs (we saw a handful of container restarts) and traffic routed to them increased error rates. hypothesis 3: routing policy/fallback didn't run for some requests because of inconsistent model tagging during the spin-up.
[02:15] Tariq: Driver OOM — are those from our model config or something Redwood-side?
[02:19] Priya: from our traces it looked like the worker containers experienced memory pressure on nvidia driver level — could be host-level memory fragmentation + large KV cache arrays. We're still digging to pin it down, could be both infra and workload shape.
[02:33] Jordan: quick interruption — one of our early mitigations was to temporarily increase per-worker cache & reduce max seq batch to limit memory churn; that helped reduce new errors but increased token cost. we can share config diffs.
[02:47] Carlos: is the caching adaptive? like if cache evictions are happening, can it reduce retention?
[02:51] Priya: currently retention policies are LRU with fixed size per worker. we have ideas — adaptive eviction thresholds and pre-warming KV cache for common prefixes. not trivial but doable.
[03:05] Aisha: about fallback — we thought Redwood had an auto-fallback to a lower-capacity variant when errors spike. we saw inconsistent behavior.
[03:12] Jordan: right, our smart routing should fallback but it requires model variants to be registered as compatible. there were a few requests routed to instances that weren't yet labeled as fallback-capable due to race during autoscale. that's on us to make the labeling more atomic.
[03:26] Maya: ok what's immediate mitigation? we need actionables we can do before another business-critical window next week.
[03:31] Jordan: short term fixes: 1) we can pin a dedicated pool for Sable for the sensitive routes to avoid noisy neighbor autoscale jitter, 2) temporarily reduce max sequence length on the route to limit per-request mem, 3) enable more aggressive health check fallback so traffic doesn't hit newly unhealthy nodes. these are config changes we can do within 24 hours.
[03:52] Carlos: pinning dedicated pool — that has cost implications. we'll need estimate.
[03:56] Liam: we'll include a cost delta in the remediation email and also a credits proposal; we recognize production impact so we'll propose a one-off credit tied to SLA window.
[04:07] Priya: verification plan — we'll run a replay of the 9/3 workload against the proposed config in a staging pool with identical traffic shape (we need Sable to provide the sample traces). we'll measure p95/p99 latency, error rates, and memory metrics. Priya will run the replay and share results.
[04:26] Carlos: we can provide the traces, but note some of them are PII — we'll send sanitized logs and a subset.
[04:33] Jordan: that works. on the longer-term reliability improvements: 1) adaptive KV cache policies, 2) better node health grading and pre-warm policy for new nodes, 3) canary release policy with traffic ramp and black/white lists, 4) improved observability: token-level SLA dashboards and clearer alerting on eviction storms.
[04:58] Maya: can you also add audit logs around model variant labeling? we need to be able to see which instance / version was labeled at what time.
[05:05] Priya: yes we can add more audit events. we also plan to surface the label propagation delay in tracing.
[05:12] Jordan: next — about SLA remediation and credits. we propose 10% monthly credit for the impacted month plus configuration/hardening work. Liam will draft a formal remediation note and numbers.
[05:22] Liam: yep I'll draft by Fri and share with Maya for approval.
[05:26] Aisha: timeline for action items?
[05:29] Jordan: quick recaps: Jordan sends timeline & raw logs by 2026-09-10; Carlos to send sanitized traces by 2026-09-09; Priya runs replays by 2026-09-12; Liam sends SLA remediation by 2026-09-11. We schedule a verification follow-up on 2026-09-14.
[05:45] Carlos: one more technical note — we saw an increase in tcp retries at the host layer during the window. could be network flaps. do you see that?
[05:53] Priya: we have some host-level network error counters that matched, yes. we'll include those metrics. possibly a cloud provider network hiccup coincident with scale events, so a multi-factor issue.
[06:07] Maya: ok final ask: we need a runbook for SRE on how to quickly mitigate if this reoccurs (steps, who's on call, toggles).
[06:16] Jordan: agreed — we'll draft a runbook with exact toggles: pin pool, reduce max seq, force-fallback toggle, and steps to roll back. we'll include direct contacts and escalation paths.
[06:25] Tariq: any blockers on Redwood side to do the quick config changes?
[06:29] Priya: nothing blocking, internal change will require a brief maintenance window for pinning pool (few mins) but non-disruptive if timed.
[06:36] Jordan: ok great. recap of next steps (quick): Jordan send timeline & logs; Carlos send sanitized traces; Priya run replays and surface results; Liam propose credits; Redwood draft runbook; schedule follow-up 2026-09-14.
[06:52] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll review once we have the replay results and decide on dedicated pool after seeing cost delta. appreciate the quick response.
[07:00] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with artifacts. end.

Notes: Transcript contains some automated transcription noise; proper nouns and acronyms may be slightly off (eg KV cache -> K V cash). Links referenced during the call: incident timeline doc (link shared in chat), replay test worksheet (shared), remediation credit proposal (to be shared).
